items.title: Evidence-based practice: Role of service evaluation in wound care
items.summary: Service evaluation has become an integral part of contemporary healthcare practice, yet it remains variably understood and inconsistently applied.

items.title: Developing a formulary to standardise practice
items.summary: The NHS Plan (2025) places a clear emphasis on delivering consistent, evidence-based and cost-effective care, with a particular focus on reducing unwarranted variation and improving patient outcomes.

items.title: Understanding research. Questionnaires 5
items.summary: In the previous papers in this mini-series (Ellis, 2025a, 2025b, 2025c, 2026), we considered the use of questionnaires as a means of collecting data for service improvement and research purposes.

items.title: Removing the barriers and reclaiming ourselves
items.summary: In my last article (Molyneux, 2026a), I explored the hidden quest of authenticity. Not only its importance to our wellbeing and mental health, but more so, the ease of denial and distortion of our internal processes and selves. I also explored how we will often be unaware that we are doing this.

items.title: Vascular reform is on the agenda. Now we need action
items.summary: It was encouraging to be in Westminster Hall this month to hear MPs debating the need for reform of vascular care. For those of us who have spent years calling for better care for people with lower-limb conditions, the fact that vascular disease was being discussed in Parliament at all, felt significant.

items.title: Lindsay Leg Clubs: People and communities at winter time: A Leg Club philosophy
items.summary: As the autumn welcomes another turn of the season, we often find a brief time to reflect on the year to date and the months ahead. The winter period can be a challenging time for people at any age across the country as the days grow shorter and the evenings darker.

items.title: Oral administration of parenteral S-ketamine in wound care when ‘conventional’ medication regimens are not sufficient: a case series
items.summary: Wound care procedures are often considered very painful. This pain can have severe effects on patients’ wellbeing and be associated with delayed wound healing. Opioids can be of use during wound care; however, they are not always sufficient.

items.title: Can the use of collagenase and hyaluronic acid gel reduce the number of repeated surgical debridements in Fournier's gangrene?
items.summary: Objective: To compare the clinical outcome criteria between treatments of repetitive mechanical debridement, conventional dressings, and the use of collagenase and hyaluronic acid gel for patients with Fournier's gangrene (FG).

items.title: Low-level laser therapy in ulcerative lesions in leprosy: a systematic review
items.summary: Objective: Leprosy is a disease that affects the peripheral nerves and ulcers are among the main complications of the disease. The laser is a tool with wide use in physiotherapy, with proven efficacy in the improvement of pressure ulcers, which creates the possibility of studies on its action in leprosy lesions.

items.title: Clinical effectiveness and safety of bacterial cellulose dressings in the management of skin wounds: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Objective: The global impact of skin injuries is substantial, compromising the wellbeing of affected individuals. Bacterial cellulose is gaining traction as a prospective dressing material due to its distinct characteristics. Nevertheless, its clinical efficacy and safety warrant detailed investigation.

items.title: Advancing healing in large hard-to-heal wounds: the ripple effect of autologous whole blood clot therapy: a case series
items.summary: Objective: Hard-to-heal (chronic) wounds of the lower extremity, particularly large-area wounds, present significant challenges due to their usually prolonged healing time and complications that might lead to surgical interventions, adding to the high burden on the healthcare system.

items.title: Nurses’ knowledge and practices regarding medical device-related pressure injuries: a cross-sectional study
items.summary: Objective: To assess accuracy of nurses’ knowledge and practices regarding medical device-related pressure injuries (MDRPIs) in Türkiye. Method: This cross-sectional study included 384 nurses who had at least one year of professional experience and were working in hospitals across different regions of Türkiye.

items.title: Effect of topical insulin in diabetic foot ulcer healing among patients with diabetes in Asia: a systematic review
items.summary: Objective: The aim of this systematic review is to provide a comprehensive understanding on the effectiveness of topical insulin in the healing of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) in patients with diabetes in Asian countries.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of pH 5.5 hypochlorous acid in the management of complex wounds in paediatric patients
items.summary: This case series describes the benefits of using of a non-cytotoxic acidic pH cleansing solution in the treatment of complex wounds in paediatric patients, at two health centres in Santiago, Chile.

items.title: Evaluation of Triketra, a chitosan-based wound healing gel, on acute/ hard-to-heal wounds: a single cohort non-comparative clinical pilot study
items.summary: Objective: This study investigated the safety and real-world effectiveness of ChitoCare Medical Triketra (Primex ehf, Iceland), a chitosan-based wound healing gel on a variety of acute and hard-to-heal wounds.

items.title: PRISM: incorporating advanced imaging technologies into a comprehensive strategy for hard-to-heal wound assessment and management
items.summary: Head-to-heal wounds—particularly diabetic lower-extremity wounds—remain among the most challenging and resource-intensive problems in contemporary healthcare, with five-year recurrence rates of 40–65% and a trajectory toward amputation that is frequently driven by three interacting and often under-recognised failures…

items.title: Conexeu progresses towards FDA submission with regenerative wound care technology
Wound scanning app helping to ‘save nurse time’
items.summary: A wound-scanning app used by district nursing teams in Wales has helped save nurse time and improve patient care. The ‘Minuteful for Wound’ app, developed by technology company Precision Health Tech, allows nurses and healthcare staff to scan and measure wounds so they can be monitored virtually.

items.title: Vacuum-assisted closure therapy in the management of patients with necrotising fasciitis
items.summary: Objective: This study aims to compare vacuum-assisted closure (VAC) and conventional wound dressings in patients with necrotising fasciitis (NF).

items.title: Rare aetiologies of leg ulcers: a prospective analysis
items.summary: Objective: As treatment guidelines differ based on the causal effects of hard-to-heal (chronic) leg ulcers, correct diagnosis is essential for the best therapeutic outcomes.

items.title: Intermittent pneumatic thigh compression for the treatment of lower limb wounds (IPCOTT): a randomised control trial
items.summary: Objective: Hard-to-heal (chronic) venous leg ulcers (VLUs) are challenging to heal with standard of care (SoC) alone.

items.title: Biomechanical influence of cavity fillers on periwound soft tissue strains in sacral pressure injuries
items.summary: Objective: Deep cavity pressure injuries (PIs) are commonly managed with wound fillers, the biomechanical role of which remains poorly understood. This study aimed to assess how the mechanical properties of filler influence periwound soft tissue strains.

items.title: Biomimetic approaches in wound healing and skin regeneration: a narrative review
items.summary: Objective: Biomimetic approaches, which mimic the structural and functional characteristics of biological tissues and natural healing processes, have emerged as a promising strategy in regenerative medicine and, in wound care, biomimetic materials are designed to replicate the extracellular matrix and wound…

items.title: Safety and cost-effectiveness of a pure hypochlorous acid cleansing solution in wounds and non-intact skin management: a narrative review
items.summary: Objective: Wound cleansing is an essential part of wound bed preparation and its importance in wound management is supported by numerous international guidelines and consensus documents. Cleansing solutions are used by healthcare professionals for wounds and non-intact skin.

items.title: Evaluating the efficacy and safety of Neothelium FT placental allograft in the management of hard-to-heal open wounds: a prospective case series
items.summary: Objective: The aetiology of hard-to-heal (chronic) wounds is usually categorised as either ‘diabetic foot’, ‘venous leg ulcer (VLU)’, ‘arterial’, ‘pressure injury’, ‘postoperative’ and ‘other’.
